headline.title: Gemini API Managed Agents: 3.6 Flash, hooks, and more
headline.summary: The Gemini API has introduced Managed Agents in its 3.6 Flash update, featuring new hooks and triggers to enhance functionality. This update aims to improve user interaction and automation capabilities within the Gemini platform.

articles.title: 5 ways AI Mode in Search helps you enjoy the real world
articles.summary: The article outlines five ways AI Mode in Search enhances real-world experiences by providing tailored information and recommendations for leisure activities. It emphasizes how AI can help users discover and engage in fun activities, ultimately enriching their everyday lives.

articles.title: 5 ways to host the ultimate dinner party with Google Search
articles.summary: The article outlines five practical tips for hosting a successful dinner party using Google Search, including menu planning, decoration ideas, and entertainment suggestions. It emphasizes leveraging online resources to enhance the overall experience for guests.

articles.title: AI’s finally expensive enough to make Wall Street nervous
articles.summary: Google has raised its spending estimate for the upcoming earnings season to between $195 billion and $205 billion, up from a previous projection of up to $190 billion. This increase has raised concerns among investors on Wall Street regarding the financial implications of rising AI costs.

articles.title: Scientific computing in the age of agentic AI
articles.summary: A recent field report highlights the integration of AI coding agents in scientific computing, which is enhancing software development and accelerating discoveries in areas such as genomics. This advancement signifies a shift in how researchers approach complex computational tasks.

articles.title: LFM2.5-Encoders for Fast Long-Context Inference on CPU
articles.summary: Researchers have developed LFM2.5-Encoders, a new architecture designed to enhance long-context inference speed on CPU systems. This advancement aims to improve the efficiency of processing lengthy sequences in various AI applications.

articles.title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises
articles.summary: Fish Audio has secured $52 million in seed funding to develop AI voice models aimed at creators and enterprises. The startup, which launched last year, currently serves over 8 million users and generates an annual recurring revenue of $21 million.

articles.title: Recursive Superintelligence signs $410M compute deal with Amazon
articles.summary: Recursive Superintelligence has signed a $410 million compute deal with Amazon to enhance its self-improving AI systems. The company aims to allocate its budget primarily towards computing resources rather than traditional operational costs to automate its product development.

articles.title: Research directions in condensation: varieties of objectivity
articles.summary: The article outlines proposed research directions in the mathematical theory of condensation, focusing on the organization of world descriptions into conceptual parts. It references existing work by Eisenstat (2025) and discusses key concepts such as random variable models and latent variable models.

articles.title: The OlmoEarth Platform: Geospatial inference at planetary scale
articles.summary: The OlmoEarth platform utilizes advanced geospatial inference techniques to analyze and interpret large-scale environmental data across the planet. This innovative tool aims to enhance decision-making in areas such as climate change, resource management, and urban planning.

articles.title: AI leaders sign statement asking the government to do something about automated AI
articles.summary: Leaders from major AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft, have signed a statement urging the US government to implement measures for regulating the development of advanced AI technologies. The statement advocates for either a slowdown in frontier AI development or an acceleration of coordinated global governance efforts to address potential risks.

articles.title: Samsung’s chip workers are jumping ship to rival SK Hynix
articles.summary: Samsung semiconductor employees are increasingly leaving the company to join rival SK Hynix, with some, like engineer Lee, actively working on their job applications during off-hours. This trend highlights growing dissatisfaction among Samsung's chip workers and the competitive hiring landscape in the semiconductor industry.
